AP33Solved: VLAN and port flags mutation/rollback scope

remainingFindings.finding: PPE currently revokes on post-change notifications. Core provides pre-change events, but failed changes may omit matching post events; a simple begin-on-pre/end-on-post counter can leak or permit republishing during rollback.
remainingFindings.nextImplementation: Review whole mutation scopes or a policy owner design; test MTU/address/upper-link success, rejection, rollback, and device close. Do not replace with polling.

remainingFindings.finding: Generic filters can mutate without RTNL. lockeddevcnt serializes driver callbacks, but skip_hw policy need not call the offload driver at all. Exact own-rule parser/readback is insufficient to prove the entire ingress/egress policy.
remainingFindings.nextImplementation: Kernel-observed TC policy lifetime/ownership must cover qdisc/filter/chain/actions and preexisting policy before an executor may publish. A dedicated non-TC publisher is a design option, not implemented or approved as a final design.

remainingFindings.finding: The ordinary unicast bridge path calls br_fdb_find_rcu and forwards an existing nonlocal entry until actual deletion; has_expired is an extra conservative check in PPE qualification. AP32 fences actual FDB deletion. An ageing-time assignment alone is not proof of a software/hardware forwarding mismatch.
remainingFindings.nextImplementation: Keep actual delete/move fence; review aging/refresh performance and hardware lease separately. Do not label an unproven cache-age root cause.
